20260827213657_AddCurrentDerivationAndCh.reason: Adds defaulted or nullable document derivation and locator columns, backfills only unambiguous current rows, and adds constraints respected by the previous indexer, which writes null pages and does not read the new columns.

20260828161744_AddPartyGuestMessages.reason: Adds two default-false Party settings and a new guest-message table; the previous application ignores the new table and continues to read and write existing rows through compatible defaults.

20260829173856_AddDocumentVisualRetrieva.reason: Creates only new visual-retrieval tables, indexes, constraints, and an optional pgvector accelerator; the previous application neither reads nor writes them.

20260830221014_AddPartyGuestHubChallenge.reason: Additive Party challenge tables, indexes, and settings with disabled/default-compatible values.

20260901134021_AddPrintFoundation.reason: Adds only new owner-scoped Print station, enrollment, device, and job tables; the previous application does not read or write them.

20260905074138_AddPartyPrintStudio.reason: Creates only the three new party-print tables — profiles, idempotency requests, and the per-job source rows; the previous application neither reads nor writes them, and no existing table is altered.

20260905080901_AddPartyPrintCapabilityTo.reason: Adds one nullable PrintTokenHash column to party_album_links and a unique index over it. The previous application leaves the column null, and PostgreSQL treats nulls as distinct in a unique index, so existing links keep working and rolling back to that application writes nothing the constraint could reject.

20260905191336_AddPartyPrintPerGuestBudg.reason: Adds four NOT NULL integer columns with defaultValue 0 — two per-guest ceilings on party_print_profiles and two per-guest print counters on party_participants. Existing rows take the default, which reads as "no per-guest limit" and "nothing printed yet"; the previous application neither reads nor writes any of them, so rolling back to it leaves the columns at values the new schema also accepts.

20260905231112_AddPartyGameRuntime.reason: Creates only the two new party game runtime tables with their indexes and check constraints; the previous application neither reads nor writes them, and no existing table, column or constraint changes.

20260906000059_AddPartyActivityRules.reason: Adds two nullable columns and one NOT NULL text column with defaultValue 'binary' to party_challenges, plus check constraints the default and the nulls both satisfy. Existing rows take values the previous application never reads or writes, so it keeps creating and editing activities exactly as before against the upgraded schema.

20260906001707_AddPartyGameVotes.reason: Creates only the new party_game_votes table with its unique and lookup indexes and a value check constraint; the previous application neither reads nor writes it, and no existing table, column or constraint changes.

20260906004257_AddPartyDisplayHeartbeat.reason: Adds one nullable timestamp column to party_album_links. Existing rows take null, which reads as 'no display has been seen'; the previous application neither reads nor writes it, so rolling back to it leaves the column at a value the new schema also accepts.

20260907104555_AddPartyGuestIdentityAndM.reason: Adds one nullable timestamp and one NOT NULL integer with defaultValue 0 to party_participants, and one NOT NULL integer with defaultValue 0 to party_album_links. Existing rows take values that read as 'not retired', 'no greetings sent' and 'no message limit', which is exactly the behaviour before the columns existed; the previous application neither reads nor writes any of them, so rolling back to it leaves values the new schema also accepts.

20260908090627_AddPendingBlobPurge.reason: Creates only the new pending_blob_purges table with its primary key and one lookup index; no existing table, column, constraint or index changes. The previous application neither reads nor writes it, and it is written only by BlobJanitor, which is disabled by default. Rolling back leaves at most a few rows the old application ignores and the new one drains on its next tick.

20260909090022_AddTvDisplayAssignment.reason: Adds two columns to tv_sessions: a NOT NULL string with defaultValue 'general' and a nullable uuid, plus an index, a restricting foreign key to party_album_links and a check constraint tying the two columns together. Every existing paired television takes 'general' with no link, which is exactly the behaviour it had before the columns existed; the previous application neither reads nor writes either column, so rolling back to it leaves values the new schema also accepts, and the check constraint holds for every row the old application could write.

20260909164555_AddPartyAggregateRoot.reason: Party becomes the aggregate root. It creates the parties and party_media_sources tables, then adds a NOT NULL PartyId to party_album_links with a restricting foreign key and backfills one party per historical party album. The previous application knows nothing about PartyId, so every link it minted after the upgrade would carry the zero GUID and be rejected by that foreign key: rolling back leaves an installation that cannot enable party mode at all. It also removes the Party/ShowOnTv coupling, which the previous application still assumes. This migration therefore requires a short maintenance window in which Party is unavailable, taken deliberately in preference to a dual-write transition spread through the services; the rest of NubArca is unaffected and no token, participant, upload, message, print, game or face-search row is read or rewritten.

20260909204649_AddPartyMainMediaSourceUn.reason: Replaces the plain party_media_sources album index with a unique index over (AlbumId, Role), making 'one album is one party's main media source' a database rule rather than an application check. No table, column or row changes. The previous application already created at most one main source per album through EnsureForAlbumAsync, so every existing row satisfies the constraint and rolling back to that application writes nothing the unique index could reject.

20260909224245_AddPartyGuestContent.reason: Creates only the new party_guest_contents table with its composite primary key and one restricting foreign key to parties. No existing table, column, constraint or index changes, and no data is written. The previous application neither reads nor writes it, so rolling back to that application leaves rows it simply ignores and writes nothing the new schema could reject.

20260910171228_AddPartyMediaReferences.reason: Adds one nullable uuid column (MediaFileItemId) to party_guest_contents, one lookup index on it and one on the existing party_challenges.MediaFileItemId, and two foreign keys to file_items with ON DELETE SET NULL. Nothing is backfilled and no existing value is rewritten. Before the party_challenges constraint is created the migration checks that every existing activity reference names a file_items row, and if one does not it raises an explicit exception inside its transaction, leaving the schema untouched; it never nulls or repairs such a reference itself. The previous application never reads or writes party_guest_contents.MediaFileItemId, so its inserts take null; it writes party_challenges.MediaFileItemId only after confirming that the owner's file exists, which the new constraint accepts; and when it permanently purges a file the database now nulls the reference instead of leaving it dangling, which that application already renders as an activity without a picture. Rolling back to it therefore leaves only values the new schema also accepts.

20260910231201_AddPartyDisplayGrant.reason: Creates only the new party_display_grants table with its primary key, one unique index on the token hash, three lookup indexes, a cascading foreign key to tv_sessions and a restricting one to party_album_links. No existing table, column, constraint or index changes. The previous application neither reads nor writes it, and it is written only by the display-grant mint, which no older client calls. Rolling back leaves at most a few short-lived rows the old application ignores; nothing else references the table, so its presence changes no existing query plan or constraint.

20260911160022_AddPartyContentMediaPrese.reason: Adds one NOT NULL character varying(16) column (MediaPresentation) to party_guest_contents with defaultValue 'inline', and one check constraint restricting it to 'inline' or 'poster'. The generated SQL is exactly two ALTER TABLE ... ADD statements: no existing row is rewritten, no other column, constraint or index changes, and nothing is backfilled. Existing rows take the default, which is precisely the presentation they were already rendered with, so the upgrade changes no guest surface. The previous application never reads or writes the column, and its inserts omit it entirely, so the database supplies 'inline' and the constraint accepts it; rolling back to that application therefore leaves only values the new schema also accepts, and leaves every row meaning what it means today.

20260913184903_AddPartyGamePlanningAndPr.reason: Three additive changes. It adds one NOT NULL boolean column (PriorityVotingEnabled) to party_album_links with defaultValue false, which is exactly the behaviour before the column existed — the previous application never reads or writes it and its inserts omit it, so the database supplies false. It creates the new party_game_exclusions table with its primary key, one unique index, one lookup index, a cascading foreign key to party_game_sessions and a restricting one to party_challenges; no existing table, column or row is touched and the previous application neither reads nor writes it. And it WIDENS the ck_party_game_sessions_phase check constraint to admit the new 'intermission' phase, by dropping and re-adding it: widening accepts every value the narrower constraint accepted, so no existing row can fail it and the previous application keeps writing the same seven phases it always wrote. A row can only reach 'intermission' if the new application put it there, which cannot happen while the old one is running; if the old image were restored while such a row existed it would read the phase as unknown and offer that control room no commands until a host advanced the game — a degraded surface, not a failed request or a rejected write.

20260914092809_AddPartyContentTextAlign.reason: Adds one NULLABLE character varying(16) column (TextAlign) to party_guest_contents with no default, and one check constraint restricting it to 'left' or 'center'. The generated SQL is exactly two ALTER TABLE ... ADD statements: no existing row is rewritten, nothing is backfilled, and no other column, constraint or index changes. Every existing row reads NULL, which the application defines as 'the surface's own default' — left in a section, centred in the thank-you — i.e. exactly how each row rendered before the column existed, so the upgrade changes no guest surface. NULL passes a CHECK by definition. The previous application never reads or writes the column and its inserts omit it, so it keeps writing NULL; rolling back to it therefore leaves only values the new schema accepts, and a host's explicit choice is merely ignored (rendered with the default) rather than causing a failed request or a rejected write.

20260914123145_AddPartyCovers.reason: Adds two NULLABLE uuid columns (InvitationCoverFileItemId, LiveCoverFileItemId) to parties with no default, one plain index on each, and one foreign key from each to file_items with ON DELETE SET NULL. No existing row is rewritten and nothing is backfilled: every existing party reads NULL for both, which the application defines as 'no cover chosen' — the invitation falls back to the album's chosen cover and the party to the album's cover, i.e. the album-derived covers these pages already used. The previous application never reads or writes either column and its inserts omit them, so it keeps writing NULL; the foreign keys constrain only values the new application writes, and SET NULL on a permanent file delete is simply a reference that no longer exists. Rolling back to the previous application therefore leaves only values the new schema accepts: a cover a host chose is ignored (and the old invitation rendering returns), never a failed request or a rejected write.

20260914135548_AddPartyContentMediaFrame.reason: Adds four NULLABLE columns to party_guest_contents with no default — MediaOrientation character varying(16), and MediaCropZoom, MediaCropCenterX and MediaCropCenterY double precision — plus two check constraints: the orientation is 'portrait' or 'landscape', and the crop lies inside the print editor's limits (zoom 1..4, centre 0..1). No existing row is rewritten and nothing is backfilled; NULL passes both constraints by definition. Every existing row reads NULL, which the application defines as 'the whole photograph' — the section photo shown at its own proportions instead of the previous fixed landscape crop, which is the rendering change this release intends. The previous application never reads or writes these columns and its inserts omit them, so it keeps writing NULL; rolling back to it leaves only values the new schema accepts, and a host's frame is merely ignored (the old landscape crop returns), never a failed request or a rejected write.

20260914171437_AddPartyContentTextPlacem.reason: Adds one NULLABLE character varying(16) column (TextPlacement) to party_guest_contents with no default, and one check constraint restricting it to 'overlay'. The generated SQL is exactly two ALTER TABLE ... ADD statements: no existing row is rewritten and nothing is backfilled. Every existing row reads NULL, which the application defines as 'the words below the photograph' — exactly how every slot rendered before the column existed — and NULL passes the constraint by definition. The previous application never reads or writes the column and its inserts omit it, so it keeps writing NULL; rolling back to it leaves only values the new schema accepts, and a host's 'on the photograph' choice is merely ignored (the words return below), never a failed request or a rejected write.

20260915121140_AddPartyGuestListRsvp.reason: The schema change is additive: it creates six new owner-private Party tables (party_invitation_groups, party_guests, party_rsvps, party_rsvp_questions, party_rsvp_answers, party_invitation_deliveries) with their indexes, check constraints and RESTRICTING foreign keys to parties and to each other, alters no existing table, column, index or constraint and backfills nothing, so the previous application can ignore the new tables during its normal reads. It is nevertheless not previous-application compatible once used: as soon as the new application has written guest-list or RSVP rows for a party, the previous application's party teardown (PartyStateEraser, shared by tearing a party down and by deleting its album) does not know these child tables, and their restricting foreign keys to parties refuse its delete. An image-only rollback to the previous backend after this migration is therefore not guaranteed safe, and the release must take the manual review path rather than the guided updater.

20260915172914_AddPartyAttendance.reason: The schema change is additive: it creates two new owner-private Party tables — party_guest_attendance (keyed by the guest, with a closed 'owner'/'invitation' Source check constraint) and party_attendance_guests (a check constraint on Version >= 1 and a non-empty Name, and a unique (PartyId, ClientRequestId) index) — each with a RESTRICTING foreign key, to party_guests and to parties respectively. It alters no existing table, column, index or constraint and backfills nothing, so the previous application can ignore the new tables during its normal reads. It is nevertheless not previous-application compatible once used: as soon as the new application has recorded an arrival, the previous application's party teardown (PartyStateEraser, shared by tearing a party down and by deleting its album), its invitation-group removal and its group edit that removes a named guest do not know these tables, and their restricting foreign keys refuse its delete of that guest or that party. Cascades are deliberately not introduced to paper over this. An image-only rollback to the previous backend after this migration is therefore not guaranteed safe, and the release must take the manual review path rather than the guided updater.

20260915224823_GeneralizePartyInvitation.reason: Adds columns, one index and check constraints to three tables the previous application already uses, and drops/re-adds one constraint only to WIDEN it. It creates no table and no foreign key, rewrites no row and backfills nothing in SQL. (1) party_invitation_deliveries gains a NOT NULL character varying(16) Channel with defaultValue 'email' — a metadata-only ADD on PostgreSQL 11+, and exactly true of every existing row, all of which are emails. The status check is widened from ('pending','sent','failed') to also admit 'shared'; three new checks hold the channel vocabulary ('email','whatsapp','copy'), bind each channel to its own statuses (email ⇔ pending/sent/failed, a share ⇔ shared) and forbid a reminder on a share. Every existing row — an email with one of the three old statuses — satisfies all of them. The previous application inserts deliveries without the Channel column, so the database supplies 'email', and it only ever writes pending, sent or failed with initial, resend or reminder: every row it can write passes every new check. It reads 'shared' rows it does not understand as not sent — its projection maps an unknown status to not_sent and its 'invited' test counts only 'sent' — which degrades what it displays for a shared group, never a request or a write. (2) party_invitation_groups, party_guests and party_attendance_guests each gain a NOT NULL text SearchText with defaultValue '' — the owner's folded search cache. The previous application neither reads nor writes it; its inserts take '' and its renames leave the old value. The new application re-derives every row whose SearchText disagrees with the fields it folds (PartySearchTextReconciler) each time the API starts, before serving, so the rows that predate the column and any row written or renamed by the previous application during a rollback are searchable again after the next start of the new image; nothing refuses or fails meanwhile. (3) A plain index ix_party_attendance_guests_party_checked_in on (PartyId, CheckedInAt, Id), which changes no constraint and no query result for the previous application. Rolling back to the previous application therefore leaves only rows and values the upgraded schema accepts, with no foreign key it does not know and no restricting delete it cannot perform.

20260917220556_AddPartyCrew.reason: Creates six new Party Crew tables (party_collaborators, party_collaborator_grants, party_collaborator_invites, party_collaborator_auth_challenges, party_crew_devices, party_collaborator_device_grants) with their indexes, closed-vocabulary, hash-length and send-budget check constraints and RESTRICTING foreign keys to parties and to each other, and adds one NULLABLE uuid column PartyCollaboratorId to audit_logs with a partial index over it and NO foreign key. The generated SQL is six CREATE TABLE statements, one metadata-only ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN, and their CREATE INDEX statements: it alters no existing column, constraint or index, rewrites no row and backfills nothing. Every existing audit row reads NULL, which the new application defines as "the actor was not a collaborator" — exactly what every row written before the column existed means. The previous application neither reads nor writes the column and its inserts omit it, so it keeps writing NULL, and it can ignore the six new tables during its normal reads. It is nevertheless not previous-application compatible once used: as soon as the new application has created a collaborator for a party, the previous application's party teardown (PartyStateEraser, shared by tearing a party down and by deleting its album) does not know party_collaborators or its children, and the restricting foreign key from party_collaborators to parties refuses its delete of that party. Cascades are deliberately not introduced to paper over this. A rollback is also a security downgrade rather than only a feature loss: party_crew_devices and party_collaborator_device_grants are live credentials the previous application cannot list, revoke or expire, because it has no Party Crew surface at all — although it also serves no /api/party-crew route, so those credentials authorize nothing while it is running. An image-only rollback to the previous backend after this migration is therefore not guaranteed safe, and the release must take the manual review path rather than the guided updater.
